reasoning_summary: Selected features prioritize stable, interpretable credit-risk signals with zero missingness and broad coverage across key semantic groups: credit score, loan terms, income capacity, bankcard capacity, revolving utilization, account opening activity, credit history length, mortgage history, recent inquiries, and exposure amounts. Preference was given to core, well-understood variables and their robust transformations (log, sqrt) to capture nonlinear effects while controlling redundancy by selecting representative aggregates and avoiding near-duplicates unless they add distinct information. Features with fixed business-rule bands are included to support stable scorecard defensibility. Interactions involving FICO, loan term, and verification status are included for their credit-risk relevance and operational durability. Leakage or brittle operational proxies were avoided. The list balances broad semantic coverage and stability to support downstream statistical selection and redundancy pruning.
